recipes.title: Pão de queijo, light
recipes.summary: Small Brazilian cheese breads with a crisp shell and a soft, stretchy centre. This lighter batch uses less cheese and oil while keeping the familiar savoury flavour.

steps.instruction: Preheat the oven to 200°C so it is fully hot before the pão de queijo goes in.
Warm the whole milk, olive oil and salt in a small saucepan until steaming but not boiling.
Pour the hot milk mixture over the tapioca flour and stir until no dry flour remains.
Leave the tapioca mixture to cool until it feels warm rather than hot to the touch.
Beat the eggs into the cooled mixture until the dough becomes smooth and sticky.
Fold the parmesan cheese through the dough until evenly distributed.
Shape the dough into twelve small balls and space them apart on a lined baking tray.
Bake until the cheese breads are puffed, dry on the outside and lightly golden underneath.

recipes.storageNotes: Best warm from the oven. Refrigerate baked breads for up to 3 days and reheat briefly in the oven. Freeze shaped unbaked balls or cooled baked breads for up to 2 months.

recipes.title: Pão de queijo
recipes.summary: Classic Brazilian cheese breads with a crisp exterior and a tender, chewy middle. Parmesan gives them a deep savoury flavour that makes them ideal for sharing.

steps.instruction: Preheat the oven to 200°C so it is fully hot before the pão de queijo goes in.
Warm the whole milk, olive oil and salt in a saucepan until steaming but not boiling.
Pour the hot milk mixture over the tapioca flour and stir until the flour is fully moistened.
Leave the tapioca mixture to cool until it is comfortably warm to the touch.
Beat the eggs into the cooled mixture until the dough looks glossy and evenly combined.
Fold the parmesan cheese through the sticky dough until evenly distributed.
Shape the dough into sixteen small balls and arrange them on a lined baking tray.
Bake until the cheese breads are puffed, lightly golden and firm on the outside.

recipes.storageNotes: Serve warm for the best chewy texture. Refrigerate for up to 3 days and reheat in a hot oven. The shaped dough balls or baked breads can be frozen for up to 2 months.

recipes.title: Pão de queijo, hearty
recipes.summary: A generous batch of Brazilian cheese breads with extra parmesan and a deeply savoury, chewy centre. They are especially good served warm for a shared afternoon snack.

steps.instruction: Preheat the oven to 200°C so it is fully hot before the pão de queijo goes in.
Warm the whole milk, olive oil and salt in a saucepan until steaming but not boiling.
Pour the hot milk mixture over the tapioca flour and stir until no dry flour remains.
Leave the tapioca mixture to cool until it feels warm rather than hot.
Beat the eggs into the cooled mixture until the dough is smooth, glossy and sticky.
Fold the parmesan cheese through the dough until every part is well seasoned.
Shape the dough into twenty small balls and arrange them with space between them on a lined tray.
Bake until the cheese breads are well puffed, golden underneath and dry on the outside.

recipes.storageNotes: Best eaten warm. Refrigerate for up to 3 days and restore the crisp shell in a hot oven. Freeze shaped dough balls or cooled baked breads for up to 2 months.

recipes.title: Ethiopian ful, light
recipes.summary: Warm fava beans simmered with tomatoes, cumin and paprika, topped with eggs, lemon and cilantro. It is a comforting Ethiopian breakfast with plenty of savoury flavour.

steps.instruction: Chop the onion, garlic and cilantro so all the fresh ingredients are ready before the pan is heated.
Heat the olive oil in a saucepan and cook the onion until soft and translucent.
Add the garlic, cumin and paprika and stir until the spices smell fragrant.
Add the tomatoes, canned, and cook until they begin to thicken into a sauce.
Stir in the fava beans and simmer gently, crushing a few beans against the side of the pan to thicken the ful.
Boil the eggs until the whites and yolks are set to your liking.
Peel and halve the eggs once they are cool enough to handle.
Spoon the ful into bowls and finish with the eggs, lemon juice and cilantro.

recipes.storageNotes: The bean mixture keeps for up to 3 days and reheats well with a splash of water. Store the boiled eggs separately when possible. Freeze only the bean mixture for up to 2 months.

recipes.title: Ethiopian ful
recipes.summary: A hearty Ethiopian breakfast of fava beans cooked with tomatoes and warming spices, finished with boiled eggs, lemon and cilantro. It is filling without being heavy.

steps.instruction: Chop the onion, garlic and cilantro so the fresh ingredients are ready before cooking begins.
Heat the olive oil in a saucepan and cook the onion until soft and translucent.
Add the garlic, cumin and paprika and stir until the spices smell warm and fragrant.
Add the tomatoes, canned, and cook until the mixture becomes slightly thick and saucy.
Stir in the fava beans and simmer gently, crushing some beans to give the ful a creamy texture.
Boil the eggs until set to your preferred consistency.
Peel and halve the eggs once they are cool enough to handle.
Divide the ful between bowls and top with the eggs, lemon juice and cilantro.

recipes.storageNotes: Refrigerate the ful for up to 3 days and reheat gently with a little water. Keep boiled eggs separate for the best texture. The bean mixture freezes well for up to 2 months.

recipes.title: Ethiopian ful, hearty
recipes.summary: A generous Ethiopian breakfast with plenty of warmly spiced fava beans and two eggs per person. Lemon and cilantro brighten the rich tomato base.

steps.instruction: Chop the onion, garlic and cilantro so every fresh ingredient is ready before the ful begins cooking.
Heat the olive oil in a saucepan and cook the onion until completely soft and translucent.
Add the garlic, cumin and paprika and stir until the spices become fragrant.
Add the tomatoes, canned, and cook until they reduce into a thick sauce.
Stir in the fava beans and simmer gently, crushing some beans until the ful becomes thick and spoonable.
Boil the eggs until the whites and yolks are set to your liking.
Peel and halve the eggs once they are cool enough to handle.
Spoon the ful into bowls and finish with the eggs, lemon juice and cilantro.

recipes.storageNotes: The ful keeps for up to 3 days and reheats well with a splash of water. Store the eggs separately if possible. Freeze the bean mixture, without the eggs and herbs, for up to 2 months.

recipes.title: Peruvian shrimp ceviche, light
recipes.summary: Chilled shrimp dressed with lime, onion and cilantro, served with sweet potato and corn. This lighter ceviche stays bright and satisfying with a generous amount of shrimp.

ingredients.name: sweet potato
ingredients.preparation: peeled and cut into thick slices

steps.instruction: Cut the sweet potato into thick, even slices so they cook at the same rate.
Simmer the sweet potato until tender enough to pierce easily with a knife, then drain it.
Cook the sweet corn in simmering water until tender, then drain it well.
Poach the shrimp in gently simmering water until pink and opaque throughout.
Chill the cooked shrimp in cold water until completely cool, then drain thoroughly.
Slice the onion as thinly as possible so it softens slightly in the lime dressing.
Chop the cilantro into small pieces without crushing the leaves.
Stir the lime, cilantro and salt together until the salt dissolves.
Toss the shrimp and onion with the lime mixture until evenly coated.
Leave the ceviche to marinate in the refrigerator until cold and well seasoned.
Serve the ceviche with the sweet potato and sweet corn arranged alongside it.

recipes.storageNotes: Best eaten on the day it is made. Refrigerate promptly and keep for no more than 1 day. The lime dressing will continue firming the shrimp, so this ceviche is not suitable for freezing.

recipes.title: Peruvian shrimp ceviche
recipes.summary: A fresh Peruvian-style ceviche with chilled shrimp, sharp lime, sliced onion and cilantro. Sweet potato and corn provide the traditional mild, comforting contrast.

ingredients.name: sweet potato
ingredients.preparation: peeled and cut into thick slices

steps.instruction: Cut the sweet potato into thick, even slices so every piece cooks at the same rate.
Simmer the sweet potato until tender enough to pierce easily with a knife, then drain it.
Cook the sweet corn in simmering water until tender, then drain it well.
Poach the shrimp in gently simmering water until pink, firm and opaque throughout.
Chill the cooked shrimp in cold water until completely cool, then drain thoroughly.
Slice the onion very thinly so it softens slightly without losing all of its bite.
Chop the cilantro into small pieces while keeping the leaves fresh and loose.
Stir the lime, cilantro and salt together until the salt has dissolved.
Toss the shrimp and onion with the lime dressing until everything is evenly coated.
Leave the ceviche to marinate in the refrigerator until chilled and well seasoned.
Serve the ceviche with the sweet potato and sweet corn arranged alongside it.

recipes.storageNotes: Serve on the day it is prepared for the best texture. Refrigerate immediately and keep for up to 1 day. Do not freeze, as both the shrimp and fresh lime dressing deteriorate.

recipes.title: Peruvian shrimp ceviche, hearty
recipes.summary: A generous Peruvian-style ceviche with extra shrimp, sweet potato and corn. The sharp lime and crisp onion keep the larger portion lively and refreshing.

ingredients.name: sweet potato
ingredients.preparation: peeled and cut into thick slices

steps.instruction: Cut the sweet potato into thick, even slices so the larger amount cooks evenly.
Simmer the sweet potato until tender enough to pierce easily with a knife, then drain it.
Cook the sweet corn in simmering water until tender, then drain it well.
Poach the shrimp in gently simmering water until pink, firm and opaque throughout.
Chill the cooked shrimp in cold water until completely cool, then drain thoroughly.
Slice the onion very thinly so it keeps a crisp texture without overpowering the ceviche.
Chop the cilantro into small pieces while keeping the leaves loose and fresh.
Stir the lime, cilantro and salt together until the salt dissolves.
Toss the shrimp and onion with the lime dressing until evenly coated.
Leave the ceviche to marinate in the refrigerator until chilled and well seasoned.
Serve the ceviche with the sweet potato and sweet corn arranged alongside it.

recipes.storageNotes: Best eaten immediately after marinating. Refrigerate any leftovers promptly and use within 1 day. The ceviche is not suitable for freezing because the shrimp will lose its texture.

recipes.title: Polish stuffed cabbage rolls, light
recipes.summary: Tender cabbage leaves wrapped around a savoury beef and rice filling, baked in a tomato sauce. The lighter version uses extra cabbage and a leaner filling without losing the comforting character.

steps.instruction: Preheat the oven to 180°C so it is ready when the cabbage rolls are assembled.
Simmer the white rice until only partly tender, then drain it so it can finish cooking inside the rolls.
Soften the green cabbage leaves in simmering water until flexible enough to roll without tearing.
Heat the olive oil in a pan and cook the onion until soft and translucent.
Add the garlic and stir until fragrant without allowing it to brown.
Combine the ground beef, white rice, cooked onion, garlic and paprika until the filling is evenly mixed.
Stir the tomatoes, canned, tomato paste and beef stock together to make the baking sauce.
Wrap portions of the beef filling tightly inside the softened cabbage leaves.
Arrange the cabbage rolls snugly in a baking dish and pour the tomato sauce around them.
Bake the covered cabbage rolls until the beef is cooked through and the cabbage is very tender.
Rest the cabbage rolls briefly so the filling firms slightly before serving.

recipes.storageNotes: Refrigerate for up to 4 days and reheat covered with some sauce to prevent drying. The cooked rolls freeze well in their sauce for up to 3 months.

recipes.title: Polish stuffed cabbage rolls
recipes.summary: Classic Polish-style cabbage rolls filled with beef and rice, then baked slowly in a rich tomato sauce. They are deeply comforting and especially good reheated the next day.

steps.instruction: Preheat the oven to 180°C so it is fully hot when the cabbage rolls are ready.
Simmer the white rice until only partly tender, then drain it so it finishes cooking in the filling.
Soften the green cabbage leaves in simmering water until flexible enough to roll easily.
Heat the olive oil in a pan and cook the onion until soft and translucent.
Add the garlic and stir until fragrant without letting it colour.
Combine the ground beef, white rice, cooked onion, garlic and paprika until evenly mixed.
Stir the tomatoes, canned, tomato paste and beef stock together to make a smooth baking sauce.
Wrap portions of the beef and rice filling tightly inside the cabbage leaves.
Arrange the cabbage rolls snugly in a baking dish and pour the tomato sauce around them.
Bake the covered cabbage rolls until the beef is cooked and the cabbage is completely tender.
Rest the cabbage rolls briefly so they hold together neatly when served.

recipes.storageNotes: Keeps very well for up to 4 days in the refrigerator. Reheat covered in the tomato sauce. Freeze cooked rolls with their sauce for up to 3 months and thaw overnight before reheating.

recipes.title: Polish stuffed cabbage rolls, hearty
recipes.summary: Generous Polish-style cabbage rolls packed with extra beef and rice and baked in plenty of tomato sauce. This larger batch makes a substantial high-protein dinner for four.

steps.instruction: Preheat the oven to 180°C so it is fully hot before the larger batch goes in.
Simmer the white rice until only partly tender, then drain it well.
Soften the green cabbage leaves in simmering water until flexible enough to wrap without tearing.
Heat the olive oil in a pan and cook the onion until soft and translucent.
Add the garlic and stir until fragrant without allowing it to brown.
Combine the ground beef, white rice, cooked onion, garlic and paprika until evenly mixed.
Stir the tomatoes, canned, tomato paste and beef stock together to make the baking sauce.
Wrap generous portions of the beef filling tightly inside the softened cabbage leaves.
Arrange the cabbage rolls snugly in a deep baking dish and pour the tomato sauce around them.
Bake the covered cabbage rolls until the beef is cooked through and the cabbage is very tender.
Rest the cabbage rolls briefly before serving so the larger fillings settle.

recipes.storageNotes: Refrigerate for up to 4 days and reheat covered in plenty of sauce. The rolls freeze well for up to 3 months; freeze them in portions with enough tomato sauce to keep them moist.

recipes.title: Buffalo chicken celery boats, light
recipes.summary: Crisp celery filled with creamy shredded buffalo chicken and a little cheddar. These American snack boats are punchy, satisfying and easy to prepare ahead.

steps.instruction: Cut the celery into short boat-shaped pieces and dry the grooves so the filling stays in place.
Heat the olive oil in a pan and cook the chicken breast, skinless, until firm and opaque throughout.
Rest the cooked breast until cool enough to handle without losing too much moisture.
Shred the chicken breast into fine pieces using two forks.
Stir the sour cream, hot sauce and paprika together until smooth.
Fold the shredded chicken, spring onions and cheddar cheese into the cream mixture.
Spoon the buffalo chicken filling into the celery boats and serve immediately.

recipes.storageNotes: The chicken filling keeps for up to 2 days in the refrigerator. Store it separately from the celery and fill the boats shortly before eating so they remain crisp. Do not freeze the assembled snack.

recipes.title: Buffalo chicken celery boats
recipes.summary: Crunchy celery boats packed with creamy buffalo chicken, cheddar and spring onions. They deliver the familiar American buffalo flavour in a neat, low-effort snack.

steps.instruction: Cut the celery into short boat-shaped pieces and dry the grooves so they hold the filling neatly.
Heat the olive oil in a pan and cook the chicken breast, skinless, until opaque and cooked through.
Rest the cooked breast until cool enough to handle and the juices have settled.
Shred the chicken breast finely using two forks.
Stir the sour cream, hot sauce and paprika together until smooth and evenly coloured.
Fold the shredded chicken, spring onions and cheddar cheese into the cream mixture.
Fill the celery boats generously with the buffalo chicken mixture and serve.

recipes.storageNotes: Refrigerate the filling for up to 2 days in a sealed container. Keep the celery separate and assemble just before serving for the best crunch. The finished boats are not suitable for freezing.

recipes.title: Buffalo chicken celery boats, hearty
recipes.summary: Generously filled celery boats with extra buffalo chicken, sour cream and cheddar. This hearty keto snack is substantial enough to share after training or between meals.

steps.instruction: Cut the celery into sturdy boat-shaped pieces and dry the grooves thoroughly.
Heat the olive oil in a pan and cook the chicken breast, skinless, until firm and opaque throughout.
Rest the cooked breast until cool enough to handle and the juices settle back into the meat.
Shred the chicken breast into fine, tender pieces using two forks.
Stir the sour cream, hot sauce and paprika together until completely smooth.
Fold the shredded chicken, spring onions and cheddar cheese into the cream mixture until evenly combined.
Pile the buffalo chicken filling into the celery boats and serve while the celery is crisp.

recipes.storageNotes: Store the buffalo chicken filling and celery separately for up to 2 days. Assemble only what you plan to eat so the celery remains crisp. Freezing is not recommended.
